title: Salt Lick, Kansas, May 1866
summary: Salt Lick is a town built on credit for a railroad that hasn't come: a hotel, a saloon, shipping pens, and two thousand Texas longhorns waiting on the prairie with nowhere to go. Be one of its people, or make your own.

playerSlot.summary: You make your own townsperson of Salt Lick, a Kansas town built on credit for a railroad that hasn't come, with Texas herds waiting on the prairie.

roles.label: Saloon keeper
roles.desc: Pours the whiskey and hears everything.

roles.label: Storekeeper
roles.desc: Sells everything on credit to people they trust.

roles.label: Deputy
roles.desc: Keeps order for the marshal or the town, for a wage.

roles.label: Drover
roles.desc: Rides herd, and waits in town for wages that don't come.

roles.label: Blacksmith
roles.desc: Shoes horses and mends wagons, and knows everyone's business.

clocks.name: The herd grounds give out
clocks.fireText: The grass east of town is eaten to the dirt; the Texans must move their herds, sell for nothing, or turn them loose on the farmers' fields.

clocks.name: The town company's creditors
clocks.fireText: A Leavenworth lawyer arrives with papers to seize the hotel, the pens and everything Amos Tull owns.

opening:
Front Street at nine in the morning: drying mud, false fronts, a dog asleep in the shade of the hotel porch. From the herd grounds east of town comes the low, endless sound of two thousand longhorns that have been waiting three weeks for a buyer.

Four Texans ride in at a walk, guns on their hips, and stop at the hitching rail of the Drovers' Rest. The sign on the marshal's door across the street says that firearms are to be checked within the town limits.

The tallest of them, Wes Calhoun, looks at the sign, then up and down the street, and grins. "Mornin'," he says to nobody in particular. "Anybody in this town buying cattle yet?"
